description: "A plain walk through one referral, before and after the entry step is handed off, and what your staff still decide."

Your front desk gets a faxed referral. Today someone reads it, opens the patient's chart, and types the details into 5 or 6 fields. Two hospital time studies put that at 10 to 12 minutes per referral, and that's before anyone fixes a typo.

## Before

A staff member reads the fax, decides whether it's complete, and enters it by hand. If a field is wrong, you usually find out later, when a claim comes back or a patient calls.

## After

Your staff still read the referral and decide what to do with it. The typing step is handed off. The software enters the approved details into the chart, then reads the saved record back to confirm each field. If anything doesn't match, it stops and asks a person before it saves.

What comes back to your team is short: a list of referrals that were entered and checked, and a smaller list that needs someone to look at it. Each entry has a record of what was typed and what the chart showed afterward.

## What it's worth

That depends on your volume and on how long your staff spend per referral today. Count a normal week's referrals and time a few of them. Multiply the two, and you'll have your own estimate to compare with ours.
